A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpurLens and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and some renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original perception and hallucination evaluations, human validation studies, prompting experiments, and vision-encoder analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds model evaluations and quantitative open-ended generation results.

M1.justification: The GPT-based cue proposal and filtering, OWLv2 scoring, image ranking, and maximum-gap selection procedures remain unchanged. Additional audited models and generation experiments do not revise SpurLens itself.

E1.justification: Appendix R adds standalone COCO image-description evaluation without naming the target object. v2 already included qualitative explanations and description-assisted binary prompting. The dataset roster is unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix N/Table 11 retains the original HardImageNet ranking and random-ranking baselines. Detector and prompting alternatives also remain unchanged. Qwen3.5 and GPT-5 are additions to the models being audited.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands to Qwen3.5-9B and appendix GPT-5 results. New Appendix R uses 'Describe this image in detail' and CHAIRs/CHAIRi scoring alongside target-object hallucination rate. Existing sampling, prompting-mitigation, and token-dropping protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix R quantitatively tests whether identified biases persist under untargeted descriptions, extending the earlier qualitative support. Appendix M also supplements the encoder/full-model comparison with rank correlation; existing ablations and robustness studies remain.

E5.justification: Appendix M adds Spearman rank-correlation estimation alongside the retained Pearson correlation. The ten-repeat encoder experiments and repeated random-ranking baseline procedure are unchanged; no additional uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds Qwen3.5 results, GPT-5 HardImageNet results, and Spearman correlation 0.48. New Table 12 reports captioning CHAIRs of 39.7/45.8, CHAIRi of 7.6/8.9, and HR of 1.4%/8.8% for low/high spuriosity. Retained class-wise scores and cues match, although new Qwen3.5 summaries conflict with appendix averages.

T1.justification: The gap definitions, scoring equations, Appendix B derivations, and formal constructions in Appendices E and P are retained. Mathematical differences are notation or typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims about recognition failures, amplified hallucination, automated cue discovery, and insufficient prompting-based mitigation.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 replaces the inference that language supervision did not significantly affect the main results with an argument that encoder-level bias makes language-only remedies insufficient. It also qualifies persistence from all cases to nearly all HardImageNet classes. The formal limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link on the first page, whereas v2 only promised a future public release. The older future-tense reproducibility statement remains. Appendix R documents the new generation prompt and scoring choices.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen Team (2026) reference supporting the Qwen3.5 evaluation. The related-work discussion and SpurLens's positioning against earlier approaches otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Prose revisions are localized, especially in Section 6.3. A new Open-Ended Generation appendix is inserted, shifting earlier Appendices R/S to S/T; the main narrative and most wording are retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR typography, wider text layout, and a substantially different title/author block, reflowing figures and tables throughout. A captioning table is added, model columns expand, and the HardImageNet PA table becomes two stacked blocks. That table also introduces incorrect HR column headings.

improvement.justification: The new captioning evaluation strengthens evidence beyond target-object questions, and the code link improves access information. However, Qwen3.5's appendix PA gaps average approximately 13.8 for COCO and 10.5 for ImageNet, reversed in Table 1. Table 2 also reports 18.8 minus 1.9 as 16.4, and Table 13 labels PA results as HR. These new reliability problems coexist with useful additions, preventing a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
